merge-images.formula:
Vertical:   width = max(w1, w2),  height = h1 + spacing + h2
Horizontal: width = w1 + spacing + w2,  height = max(h1, h2)
howTo: Choose the first image with the top file picker, then the second image with the bottom one.
Pick Vertical to stack the photos, or Horizontal to place them side by side.
Set the alignment for the smaller image and adjust the spacing between them if you want a gap.
Choose a background color for the empty areas and the gap, then pick PNG or JPG output.
Press Download to save the merged image to your device.
keyFacts: Vertical mode stacks image B below image A; the output width is the wider of the two images.
Horizontal mode places image B to the right of image A; the output height is the taller of the two.
The smaller image is positioned with your chosen alignment: start, center, or end along the cross axis.
Spacing inserts a gap of 0 to 100 pixels between the images, filled with your background color.
The preview is re-rendered instantly every time you change a setting; nothing is uploaded anywhere.

limitations: Merges exactly two images at a time; for larger collages, merge pairs repeatedly.
Images are placed at their original pixel size — the tool does not resize them to match.
Very large images (above about 8000 px per side) may be slow on older phones.
EXIF metadata from the originals is not carried into the merged file.

merge-images.quickAnswer: Upload two images and pick a vertical or horizontal layout. The tool places both photos on one canvas using your alignment, spacing, and background color, then lets you download the merged result as PNG or JPG — everything happens in your browser.

merge-images.workedExample:
Two photos, each 800 × 600 px, merged vertically with 20 px spacing:
output width = max(800, 800) = 800 px
output height = 600 + 20 + 600 = 1220 px
The result is a single 800 × 1220 px image. Merged horizontally with the same spacing, it would be 800 + 20 + 800 = 1620 px wide and max(600, 600) = 600 px tall.
